Accursed Thing
uh-KUR-sid thing
noun
From accursed; the Hebrew cherem, a thing devoted to destruction and forbidden to Israel, as in the sin of Achan (Jos 7).

📖 Biblical Definition

The accursed thing is the rendering of the Hebrew cherem, a thing devoted to destruction and under the ban—set apart by the LORD for ruin, and forbidden to be taken or kept. At the fall of Jericho the LORD commanded that the city and all its spoil be wholly devoted: the silver and gold to the treasury of the LORD, and all else destroyed, and that Israel keep themselves from the accursed thing lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it. But Achan took of the accursed thing—a goodly Babylonish garment, silver, and a wedge of gold—and hid them in his tent; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against all Israel, so that they were smitten before the men of Ai. Israel could not stand before their enemies until the sin was found out and purged. The accursed thing teaches that the sin of one may bring guilt and chastisement upon the whole people, that what God has devoted to destruction is deadly to covet and keep, and that hidden sin must be brought to light and put away before the people of God can prosper. It is a type of the sin that troubles the camp, the secret covetousness that defiles the whole. The dictionary honors this record as a solemn lesson in corporate holiness, the danger of covetousness, and the necessity of putting away sin from the midst of God’s people, that the LORD may be with them in the day of battle.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The Hebrew cherem, a thing devoted to destruction and banned to Israel; Achan’s theft of it troubled the whole camp, teaching corporate holiness and the peril of hidden sin.

ACCURSED THING, Hebrew cherem, a thing devoted to destruction.

At Jericho, all the spoil was devoted; Israel was to keep from it.

Achan took of the accursed thing and hid it in his tent.

The LORD’s anger fell on all Israel; they were smitten at Ai.

A lesson in corporate holiness and the peril of hidden sin.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 7:1 — "But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel."

Jos 7:11 — "Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff."

Jos 7:13 — "Up, sanctify the people, and say, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow: for thus saith the LORD God of Israel, There is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel: thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you."

Jos 6:18 — "And ye, in any wise keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing, and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The account is judged unfair for punishing the many for one man’s sin; Scripture teaches corporate holiness and the deadly defilement of hidden, covetous sin.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the modern objection that it was unjust for Israel to suffer, and Achan’s household to perish, for one man’s sin—the protest of an individualism that denies any corporate solidarity in guilt or grace. But Scripture everywhere knows the solidarity of a people: in Adam all sinned, in Achan all Israel was troubled. The sin of one devoted thing taken made the whole camp accursed, so that Israel could not stand before their enemies (Jos 7:13).

The principle to recover is corporate holiness and the deadly nature of hidden sin. The LORD had warned Israel to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it (Jos 6:18); Achan’s secret covetousness defiled the whole. The lesson is not that God is unjust but that sin among the people of God is a serious and infectious thing, that hidden sin must be brought to light and put away, and that the camp cannot prosper while it harbours what God has cursed. It is a type of the covetousness and concealed sin that still troubles the church, and a summons to put away the accursed thing, that the LORD may be with His people.
